domain: Monetary Economics / Technology Governance / Political Economy
topic_summary: Analysis of cryptocurrency as a contested kernel read through three interpretive frameworks: sound-money (Austrian economics inflation hedge), speculative-asset (tradable commodity with no fundamental anchor), and decentralization-ideology (anti-state coordination substrate). The kernel contest centers on whether these are three readings of one shared commitment or three distinct kernels sharing only a name.

key_entities: Bitcoin/cryptocurrency protocols (technical substrate claimed by all three readings)
Sound-money advocates (Austrian economics, inflation hedge framing)
Speculative traders (price-action participants, no fundamental commitment)
Central banks (fiat money issuers, inflation policy authority)
key_tensions: Fixed supply (21M BTC cap) vs price volatility (undermines medium-of-exchange function)
Censorship-resistance claims vs regulatory capture via exchange chokepoints
Store-of-value narrative vs empirical correlation with risk-on equity markets
key_mechanisms: Proof-of-work mining (consensus mechanism anchoring decentralization claim)
Exchange-based price discovery (market mechanism linking all three readings to USD valuation)
Regulatory arbitrage (jurisdictional shopping enabling both ideology and speculation)
Narrative contagion (how readings recruit participants and shape protocol governance)
key_absences: Medium-of-exchange function (conspicuously absent from all three readings despite original whitepaper framing)
Energy cost accounting (proof-of-work externality unaddressed in sound-money economic analysis)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Cryptocurrency protocols (specifically Bitcoin) as shared substrate claimed by three incompatible interpretive frameworks
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: No single authority; interpretive legitimacy contested between Austrian economists, traders, and cypherpunks; each reading attempts to claim definitional authority
commitment_system_recognition.kernel_coherence_analysis: FAILED coherence test. The three supposed readings do NOT share a common substrate commitment. Sound-money reading grounds legitimacy in scarcity economics (21M cap as fundamental constraint). Speculative-asset reading treats protocol as price-generation mechanism with no fundamental anchor. Decentralization reading grounds legitimacy in censorship-resistance (proof-of-work consensus as irreducible substrate). These are THREE DISTINCT KERNELS sharing only a name and technical implementation. A single coherent framework cannot hold 'inflation hedge via scarcity' AND 'no fundamental value anchor' simultaneously. The supposed kernel is actually a BRANDING COLLISION of three separate commitment systems using the same technical artifact for incompatible purposes. Decomposing as three flat axes (not readings) because there is no shared interpretive substrate to contest—only a naming collision masking structural incompatibility.

omegas.description: The three supposed readings FAIL the coherence test. Sound-money requires fundamental scarcity anchor. Speculative-asset denies fundamental anchor exists. Decentralization treats protocol-level censorship-resistance as the fundamental anchor. These are not three readings of one kernel—they are three DISTINCT kernels in a branding collision. A framework holding 'inflation hedge via scarcity' cannot simultaneously hold 'no fundamental value exists.' The shared technical artifact (Bitcoin protocol) is just implementation detail, not shared commitment substrate.
omegas.source: §1.3-K kernel/reading decomposition analysis; commitment_system_recognition coherence test

omegas.description: Original Bitcoin whitepaper framed cryptocurrency as peer-to-peer electronic cash (medium-of-exchange function). All three axes analyzed here treat exchange function as ABSENT. Speculative volatility directly contradicts medium-of-exchange viability. Is this absence a collapsed fourth kernel or evidence that the medium-of-exchange reading was never structurally viable?
omegas.source: Extraction absence inventory; Dark Matter Probe 2

omegas.description: Decentralization axis assumes proof-of-work mining remains distributed. Empirical hash rate concentration in ~5 mining pools contradicts censorship-resistance claim. Is the decentralization reading a Rope (coordination still functional) or Piton (decentralization claim atrophied, extraction via concentrated mining power)?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) applied to decentralization axis

omegas.description: Speculative-asset price discovery depends on Tether (USDT) stablecoin as primary trading pair. Tether claims USD backing but lacks transparent audit. If Tether is fractional-reserve or unbacked, the speculative axis collapses into a Ponzi snare with crypto exchanges as primary beneficiaries. Beyond model's audit competence but structurally critical.
omegas.source: F34 epistemic trespass boundary; absence inventory (Tether backing not addressed in extraction)
